reason: The cited evidence shows that aging at 750°C produces γ' precipitates and increases yield strength in an Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Ti alloy, but Ti is a minor addition (5.6 at%), not a primary constituent, so the key premise that this mechanism works in a Ti-Ni-primary HEA is unsupported. The evidence also does not describe a two-stage treatment or demonstrate a fine, uniform dispersion.
premises: Aging at ~750°C can produce γ'-like coherent precipitates in a multi-element alloy containing Ni, Ti, Al, Co, Cr, Fe
These precipitates increase yield strength via precipitation strengthening
The cited alloy is a high-entropy alloy with Ni and Ti as major constituents
A two-stage heat treatment (solution anneal + age) will produce a fine, uniform dispersion of coherent precipitates in a Ti-Ni-primary HEA
